reasoning: The evidence shows South Korea's total fertility rate (TFR) increased from 0.72 in 2023 to 0.75 in 2024, exceeding the 0.72 threshold. Multiple 2025 data points indicate continued growth: Q2 2025 TFR reached 0.76, July 2025 reached 0.80, and births have risen for 13+ consecutive months with 7.2-7.4% year-over-year growth in early 2025. Experts project 2025 TFR could reach 0.8. Key drivers include increased marriages (16+ consecutive months of growth), larger cohorts of women in their 30s, expanded child-benefit policies, and shifting attitudes toward childbirth. While structural challenges remain (high maternal age, low second/third births), the trajectory strongly suggests 2025 TFR will exceed 0.72. The martial law event (December 2024) appears to have had minimal direct impact on these demographic trends, which are driven by policy changes and demographic composition.
